spec_used: specs/ocr/biology-b-21c-J257.md (+ specs/ocr/biology-b-21c-J257-bold.md as the tier authority)

assessment_verified.structure: Foundation Tier: Breadth in biology (J257/01) and Depth in biology (J257/02). Higher Tier: Breadth (J257/03) and Depth (J257/04). Learners are entered for one tier only.
assessment_verified.chapter_coverage: Both papers assess content from all eight teaching chapters (B1-B6 science content, B7 Ideas about Science, B8 Practical Skills). There is no chapter-to-paper split.
assessment_verified.paper_difference: The Breadth paper carries short answer, structured, calculation and practical-skills questions and no extended response. The Depth paper carries the same question types plus at least two 6-mark extended responses.
assessment_verified.practical_skills: At least 15% of the questions assess practical skills. Practical activities are PAGs (this chapter cites PAG1, microscopy).
assessment_verified.unit_mapping: This unit is Chapter B1 'You and your genes', topics B1.1 (what is the genome and what does it do), B1.2 (how is genetic information inherited) and B1.3 (how can and should gene technology be used). There is no B1.4. Lesson 1 covers B1.1.1-B1.1.9, lesson 2 covers B1.2.1-B1.2.8, lesson 3 covers B1.1.10-B1.1.12, lesson 4 covers B1.3.1-B1.3.4.
assessment_verified.separate_only_content_present: Yes. B1.1.7-B1.1.12 (nucleotide structure, triplet code, protein synthesis, mutations and coding/non-coding variants) and B1.2.7 (Mendel plus genome sequencing) are separate-science-only and are all taught, in lessons 1, 2 and 3. B1.3 carries no separate-only tag.

findings.claim: The <dfn> tooltip defining a gene sits inside the higher-only wrapper on the 'Genes and Proteins' collapsible, so Foundation students lose it.
findings.truth: No mark-affecting gap: paragraph n7 states outside the wrapper that a gene is the section of DNA carrying the code for a specific protein, and the glossary list carries the same definition. Narrowing the wrapper would need paragraph n8 split in two, which would change the narration block count.
findings.evidence: spec B1.1.5 (explain the terms chromosome, gene, allele, variant, genotype and phenotype) is not bold, so it is both tiers; B1.1.8 (triplet code), which fills the rest of n8, is bold.

findings.claim: 'Explain the role of mRNA in protein synthesis.' is set with no tier flag in a both-tier lesson.
findings.truth: The item tests Higher-tier-only content and must carry the (Higher tier) prefix.
findings.evidence: spec B1.1.9 (recall a simple description of protein synthesis: mRNA copy, travel to ribosome, ribosome joins amino acids) is bold, so Higher tier only, and separate science only.

findings.claim: Two knowledge checks (three bases per amino acid; mRNA copy made in the nucleus) carry no tier flag.
findings.truth: Both test Higher-tier-only outcomes and need the (Higher tier) prefix. The answer keys themselves are correct (option index 2 = '3'; option index 1 = 'mRNA').
findings.evidence: spec B1.1.8 and B1.1.9 are bold.

findings.claim: Four flashcards (triplet code, where mRNA is made, where mRNA travels, what the ribosome does) carry no tier tag, while the non-coding DNA card in the same deck does.
findings.truth: Tag the four at the end of the question, matching the deck's existing pattern.
findings.evidence: spec B1.1.8 and B1.1.9 are bold.

findings.claim: Takeaway n23 runs both-tier content (DNA as a polymer of four nucleotides) straight into Higher-only content (triplet code, mRNA, ribosomes) with no flag.
findings.truth: Tag the Higher half inline. A wrapper cannot go inside the <ul>.
findings.evidence: spec B1.1.3 and B1.1.7 are not bold; B1.1.8 and B1.1.9 are.

findings.claim: Question 5 is labelled '1 mark - Recall' but asks for two separate points (homozygous/heterozygous, and which phenotype is expressed); its own scheme says 'Both points required for the mark'.
findings.truth: 2 marks would be the usual allocation, but a 1-mark two-part item is not impossible and nothing in the spec settles it. Not edited.
findings.evidence: spec assessment section: mark allocations are not prescribed per outcome.

findings.claim: A higher-only wrapper hides the whole opening paragraph, including the <dfn> definition of a mutation and the statement that mutations are the source of all genetic variants. Foundation students see the lesson start at 'There are three main types of mutation'.
findings.truth: Foundation students of this qualification do need this: the wrapper must come off. The mutation types that follow are the Higher-only part.
findings.evidence: spec B6.1.2 ('recall that genetic variants arise from mutations, and that most have no effect on the phenotype') is NOT bold, so it is assessed at both tiers; the CSS rule body.tier-foundation .higher-only sets display:none, so wrapped text is not merely badged, it is removed.

findings.claim: The three named mutation types (substitution, insertion, deletion) and the frameshift key fact are taught unwrapped in a both-tier lesson.
findings.truth: They are Higher-tier-only content and need a higher-only wrapper.
findings.evidence: spec B1.1 narrative 'The order of bases in DNA can be changed if one or more nucleotides is deleted, inserted or substituted...' is bold, and is the only place the spec names the mutation types; B1.1.10 is bold.

findings.claim: Non-coding DNA, gene expression and the key fact on non-coding mutations are taught unwrapped, while the single paragraph between them is wrapped.
findings.truth: The whole run is Higher-tier only; wrap it as one block (and drop the inner wrapper, so one Higher Tier badge shows instead of three).
findings.evidence: spec B1.1.12 (describe how genetic variants in non-coding DNA may influence phenotype by altering how genes are expressed) is bold; 'gene expression' and 'non-coding' appear nowhere else in the spec.

findings.claim: Question 6 is labelled '1 mark - Recall' but asks for a definition and a mechanism; its own scheme says 'Both points needed for full credit'.
findings.truth: 2 marks would be the usual allocation. Same pattern as F6. Not edited.
findings.evidence: spec assessment section: mark allocations are not prescribed per outcome.

findings.claim: Three practice questions (substitution vs insertion; non-coding DNA and phenotype; a variant in a regulatory region) carry no tier flag, while a fourth in the same set is already marked (HT).
findings.truth: All three test Higher-tier-only outcomes and need the (Higher tier) prefix.
findings.evidence: spec B1.1.10-12 are bold.

findings.claim: All five knowledge checks test Higher-tier-only content with no tier flag.
findings.truth: Prefix each with (Higher tier). The answer keys are correct: insertion (index 1), 'controls gene expression' (index 1), insertion (index 2), gene (index 1), and the match order [2,0,1] pairs each mutation type with the right description.
findings.evidence: spec B1.1.10-12 are bold; knowledge checks are not tier-filtered in the player, so the text tag is the only signal a student gets.

findings.claim: Five flashcards (substitution, frameshift, what non-coding DNA does, non-coding mutation and phenotype, gene expression) carry no tier tag.
findings.truth: Tag them at the end of the question. The remaining seven cards stay untagged: what a mutation is, most mutations being neutral and variants arising from mutations are B6.1.2, which is both tiers.
findings.evidence: spec B1.1.10-12 are bold; B6.1.2 is not.

findings.claim: All three takeaways state Higher-only content with no flag.
findings.truth: Tag them: inline after the first sentence of takeaway 1 (that sentence is B6.1.2, both tiers), and as a prefix on takeaways 2 and 3.
findings.evidence: spec B1.1.10-12 are bold; B6.1.2 is not.

findings.claim: 'Describe the main steps in the process of genetic engineering.' is typed '4 marks - Required Practical Method'.
findings.truth: Wrong on two counts: this board calls its practical activities PAGs, not required practicals, and genetic engineering is not a practical activity in the first place. Retype as '4 marks - Describe a Process', a type already used elsewhere in this unit.
findings.evidence: spec practical-skills section: 'Within the specification there are a number of practicals, indicated as, for example, PAG1'. 'Required practical' is AQA and Edexcel wording. B1.1 lists PAG1 (light microscope) as this chapter's only practical.

findings.claim: Two practice questions (the main steps of genetic engineering; the plasmid as a vector) carry no tier flag.
findings.truth: Both test Higher-tier-only content and need the (Higher tier) prefix.
findings.evidence: spec B1.3.3 (describe the main steps in the process of genetic engineering, including isolating the gene, putting it into a vector, inserting it into cells and selecting modified cells) is bold. B1.3.2, the definition of genetic engineering, is not bold and stays untagged.

findings.claim: Two knowledge checks (which vector is commonly used; the gene is inserted into a _____) carry no tier flag.
findings.truth: Prefix both with (Higher tier). The answer keys are correct: 'A bacterial plasmid' (index 1) and 'vector' (index 2). The other three checks are both-tier and stay as they are; the match order [1,0,2] is right.
findings.evidence: spec B1.3.3 is bold.

findings.claim: Two flashcards (what a vector is; the four steps in order) carry no tier tag.
findings.truth: Tag them at the end. 'What is a plasmid?' stays untagged: B1.1.1a names plasmids as prokaryotic genetic material at both tiers.
findings.evidence: spec B1.3.3 is bold; B1.1.1a is not.

findings.claim: Takeaway n27 defines genetic engineering (both tiers) and then lists the four steps (Higher only) in one unflagged sentence.
findings.truth: Split the sentence and tag the steps inline.
findings.evidence: spec B1.3.2 is not bold; B1.3.3 is.

findings.claim: B1.1.1b, 'describe how to use a light microscope to observe a variety of plant and animal cells' (PAG1), is taught nowhere in the unit. No lesson mentions a microscope, and the chapter's second listed practical, extracting DNA from plant tissue, is also absent.
findings.truth: This is a both-tier assessable outcome and the spec guarantees that at least 15% of paper marks assess practical skills. Options: (a) add a short practical section to lesson 1 covering slide preparation, staining, magnification and the safety point, plus one PAG-flavoured practice question; (b) accept the gap if microscopy is taught in the science practical-skills unit elsewhere in this subject. Recommend (a): it is one section in lesson 1 and it closes an assessable outcome.
findings.evidence: spec B1.1.1b with PAG1; practical work list for B1.1 ('use a microscope to look at a variety of plant and animal cells', 'extract DNA from plant tissue'); assessment section: 'No less than 15% of the questions will assess practical skills'.

findings.claim: Lesson 2 teaches Punnett squares as the only genetic diagram. Family trees are never shown.
findings.truth: The spec names both. Recommend adding a short family-tree (pedigree) worked example to lesson 2, with one practice question that reads carrier status off a chart. It is the diagram most often set on inheritance questions and it also carries the recessive-carrier idea that lesson 4 relies on.
findings.evidence: spec B1.2 narrative: 'Genetic diagrams such as family trees and Punnett squares can be used to model and predict outcomes'; B1.2.2 requires 'use of genetic diagrams'; the IaS3 linked opportunity names family trees explicitly. Neither is bold, so this is both tiers.

findings.claim: 'Variant' is used in lesson 1 ('genetic variants set the potential') and defined nowhere in the unit until lesson 3's mutation definition.
findings.truth: B1.1.5 lists 'variant' among the terms learners must be able to explain. A single clause in lesson 1 would close it, but the term is used in context often enough that the gap is unlikely to cost marks.
findings.evidence: spec B1.1.5 (not bold, so both tiers); spec B1.1 narrative: 'A different version of a gene is a genetic variant'.

summary: Four lessons checked against J257 chapter B1. No factual errors: every Punnett square, ratio and probability recomputes correctly, all twenty knowledge-check answer keys are right, the four match items pair correctly, and Mendel, sickle cell, insulin, Golden Rice and the GM mosquito programmes are accurately described. The unit's fault is tier flagging. Under J257 the mutation and gene-technology mechanism outcomes (B1.1.8-12, B1.3.3) are bold and therefore Higher tier only, and .higher-only is display:none for Foundation students, not a badge. Lesson 3 had it backwards on both counts: the both-tier definition of a mutation was hidden from Foundation, while the mutation types, non-coding DNA and gene expression were shown to everyone. 40 edits fix the wrappers and tag 25 assessment items and takeaways. One wording error: a genetic-engineering question typed as a 'Required Practical Method' (AQA/Edexcel wording, and not a practical). Two coverage gaps referred up: PAG1 microscopy (B1.1.1b) and family trees (B1.2.2) are taught nowhere.
